mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the unemployment rate increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts by more than 10% in a month suggests a decline in demand for new homes, which is a leading indicator of a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where housing starts decreased by more than 10% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where industrial production increased by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (PCE) over three months indicates strong consumer demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings benefit from increased sales.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where real personal consumption expenditures increased over three months.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k & UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% in a quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where GDP decreased by more than 0.5% in a quarter.
